items.title: VoteVets Spends Millions to Elect Democrats, Shaping Midterms
items.author: Annie Karni
items.content: <article>The organization, founded in 2006 to back Democratic veterans opposing the Iraq war, is pouring huge sums into this year’s elections amid intense voter antipathy for another conflict in the Middle East.</article>

items.title: ‘Zombified’ C.D.C., Hobbled by Cuts, Struggles to Fulfill Scientific Mission
items.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
items.content: <article>The agency has lost its independence and nearly a third of its staff, as Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and associates have tightened control.</article>

items.title: Bobby Pulido, a Texan Singer, Puts Republicans on Defense
items.author: Bayliss Wagner
items.content: <article>Bobby Pulido, a Tejano musician running as a Democrat for the House, has left his Republican opponent struggling to match his star power in a district that President Trump won easily in 2024.</article>

items.title: A 7-Day Standoff That Said So Much About Trump and the Media
items.author: Michael M. Grynbaum
items.content: <article>An abrupt decree, a network boycott, a legal intervention and an uneasy détente: This was no typical battle between a president and his press corps.</article>

items.title: Rahm Emanuel Makes His 2026 Play
items.author: Shane Goldmacher
items.content: <article>The longtime Democratic insider has emerged as a behind-the-scenes force in his party’s push to win back Congress. After that, he’ll think about 2028.</article>

items.title: U.S. Rejects U.N. Declaration on Preparing for Future Pandemics
items.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
items.content: <article>Most member nations spoke in support of the declaration, but some rich countries had strong objections.</article>

items.title: Trump Proposes $810 Million in Education and Health Cuts, Defying Congress
items.author: Catie Edmondson
items.content: <article>The attempted clawback represents the second time in as many years that the White House has sought to cancel funding approved by lawmakers.</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Ruling Could Have Limited Impact on Voter Screening in Midterms
items.author: Richard Fausset, Nick Corasaniti and Julie Bosman
items.content: <article>Federal law requires a 90-day “quiet period” before elections, likely restricting the immediate scope of a decision that allows the use of a citizenship database to examine voter rolls.</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Once Again Blocks Republican-Backed Voting Map in Missouri
items.author: Ann E. Marimow and Mitch Smith
items.content: <article>A federal appeals court had sided with Republicans seeking to use redrawn congressional district boundaries to give their party an advantage in the midterms elections.</article>

items.title: As Xi Leaves Washington, Divisions Still Simmer Beneath the Surface
items.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs and David E. Sanger
items.content: <article>President Trump welcomed Xi Jinping of China for a state visit that was heavy on pomp and ceremony. But surprisingly little time was spent on the issues that most divide the two superpowers.</article>

items.title: China’s Xi Snubs a Troubled U.N. for Trump, Overshadowing Its Big Week
items.author: Michael Crowley
items.content: <article>The U.S.-China summit offered a sharp contrast with the action at the faltering United Nations in a gridlocked New York.</article>

items.title: ICE Raids in Beef Country Raise Fears of Higher Prices
items.author: Kevin Draper and J. David Goodman
items.content: <article>Cattle industry groups in Texas, Oklahoma and Kansas and two Republican senators said the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement actions were hurting operations.</article>

items.title: Saudi Arabia Open to Possibly Developing Nuclear Weapons
items.author: Julian E. Barnes and Robert Jimison
items.content: <article>An intelligence assessment examined Saudi Arabia’s military ambitions as Congress reviews a new civilian nuclear deal between the U.S. and the kingdom.</article>

items.title: Latest Midterm Polls Reveal Bright Spots for Republicans
items.author: Ruth Igielnik
items.content: <article>There has been a turnaround in Maine, our new poll shows.</article>

items.title: Bracing for Midterm Losses, Republicans in Congress Try a Pre-election Pivot
items.author: Annie Karni and Carl Hulse
items.content: <article>After nearly two years of allowing President Trump to set their agenda, G.O.P. senators are grasping for some quick action on cost-of-living measures they can show voters before November.</article>

items.title: Supreme Court Allows Use of Trump Administration’s Expansive Database for Voter Screening
items.author: Abbie VanSickle
items.content: <article>Critics of a citizenship database built by the Trump administration have raised alarms about privacy and improper voter purges.</article>

items.title: Here’s How Trump Is Building a National Citizenship Database to Check Voters
items.author: Nicholas Nehamas and Zach Montague
items.content: <article>The Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to deploy a system that merges personal data from across the government. Questions remain about its reliability.</article>

items.title: After Tough Primaries, Democrats in Key States Feel Unified, New Polls Find
items.author: Ruth Igielnik and Lisa Lerer
items.content: <article>A majority of Democrats in Maine and Michigan said the primary process strengthened their party heading into November.</article>

items.title: Not Long Ago, Trump Accused China of Election Meddling. Today, ‘Great Friendship.’
items.author: Zolan Kanno-Youngs
items.content: <article>President Trump softened much of his stance toward China as he prepared to host its leader. But his disregard of a topic that has consumed him — the 2020 election — was particularly stark.</article>

items.title: At State Dinner for China’s Leader, Melania Trump Wears the Pants
items.author: Vanessa Friedman
items.content: <article>And possibly makes history while doing so.</article>
